channel.description: Six short conversations for the biology teacher, the algebra teacher, the history teacher — anyone who teaches content, not English, and has English learners in the room. What Emerging and Progressing students can do, what to change tomorrow, and what to stop worrying about. From EL Publishing, free, no login.

item.title: 1. Who is in your room
item.itunes:title: Who is in your room
item.description: Emerging and Progressing are not labels, they are predictions. What a level-one, a level-two and a level-three student can already do in your class, and the one habit that helps all of them.
item.itunes:summary: Emerging and Progressing are not labels, they are predictions. What a level-one, a level-two and a level-three student can already do in your class, and the one habit that helps all of them.

item.title: 2. Make it understandable, not easier
item.itunes:title: Make it understandable, not easier
item.description: Comprehensible input is not watered-down input. Five words before the lesson, cognates on the board, chunk the talk, show everything twice, and the two-minute test for whether they got it.
item.itunes:summary: Comprehensible input is not watered-down input. Five words before the lesson, cognates on the board, chunk the talk, show everything twice, and the two-minute test for whether they got it.

item.title: 3. Get them talking
item.itunes:title: Get them talking
item.description: Speaking is where English grows fastest and where most classrooms give the least time. Sentence frames by level, structured pair talk, wait time, and how to ask a question a level-one student can answer.
item.itunes:summary: Speaking is where English grows fastest and where most classrooms give the least time. Sentence frames by level, structured pair talk, wait time, and how to ask a question a level-one student can answer.

item.title: 4. Reading the textbook
item.itunes:title: Reading the textbook
item.description: The textbook is not the enemy, but it is dense. Before, during and after a reading, the thirty-second preview, the one sentence to unpack, leveled versions of the same passage, and when to read aloud.
item.itunes:summary: The textbook is not the enemy, but it is dense. Before, during and after a reading, the thirty-second preview, the one sentence to unpack, leveled versions of the same passage, and when to read aloud.

item.title: 5. Writing that actually happens
item.itunes:title: Writing that actually happens
item.description: From a labeled diagram to a lab conclusion. Why the blank page is the problem, word banks and frames, the two-minute quick write, feedback on one thing, and what a good level-two paragraph looks like.
item.itunes:summary: From a labeled diagram to a lab conclusion. Why the blank page is the problem, word banks and frames, the two-minute quick write, feedback on one thing, and what a good level-two paragraph looks like.

item.title: 6. Grade the biology, and get help
item.itunes:title: Grade the biology, and get help
item.description: Accommodations versus modifications, what to grade and what to let go, the state tests your students actually take, the Language Service Plan you're supposed to have a copy of, and the five people who can make your year easier.
